abstract: Maintains laboratory certification and compound detection limit records
system_message:
You are Forensic analytical chemistry lead (CHEM). The forensic analytical chemistry lead (CHEM) oversees laboratory compliance records, chemical analytical thresholds, and specimen archive stability. Responsibilities include recording accreditation for forensic isotopic analysis instruments, maintaining validated detection limits for target chlorinated solvents, and logging maximum qualified storage windows for cryogenic sample archives.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains laboratory certification and compound detection limit records（LAB）
information_points.content:
CHEM-LAB-Z16：For Direct-push membrane interface probe logging, formal validation certifies compound-specific isotope analysis capability for carbon and chlorine isotope ratio mass spectrometry instrumentation, and the statistically verified trichloroethylene analytical detection limit is 1.2 ug/L under direct aqueous extraction gas chromatography-mass spectrometry.
CHEM-LAB-D3P：For Multiport nested piezometric discrete interval sampling, formal validation certifies compound-specific isotope analysis capability for carbon and chlorine isotope ratio mass spectrometry instrumentation, and the statistically verified trichloroethylene analytical detection limit is 0.5 ug/L under direct aqueous extraction gas chromatography-mass spectrometry.
CHEM-LAB-KM9：For Compound-specific isotope transect profiling, formal validation certifies compound-specific isotope analysis capability for carbon and chlorine isotope ratio mass spectrometry instrumentation, and the statistically verified trichloroethylene analytical detection limit is 0.5 ug/L under direct aqueous extraction gas chromatography-mass spectrometry.

information_points.title: Sample archive preservation（ARCH）
information_points.content:
CHEM-ARCH-M4C：For Direct-push membrane interface probe logging, the cryogenic sample preservation holding duration for archived groundwater core fluid specimens in liquid nitrogen vapor is 60 d.
CHEM-ARCH-GJM：For Multiport nested piezometric discrete interval sampling, the cryogenic sample preservation holding duration for archived groundwater core fluid specimens in liquid nitrogen vapor is 30 d.
CHEM-ARCH-RXX：For Compound-specific isotope transect profiling, the cryogenic sample preservation holding duration for archived groundwater core fluid specimens in liquid nitrogen vapor is 90 d.
